question: Should OpenClaw accept this Vault resolver as a bundled core plugin with Gateway-runtime Vault credentials, network reads, plugin activation mutation, and dependency graph changes?
rationale: The implementation uses an existing SecretRef pluginIntegration seam, but accepting a bundled Vault resolver changes the trusted credential boundary and core/plugin ownership in a way automation cannot decide.

options.title: Clean and security-approve before merge
options.body: Remove the unrelated shrinkwrap bumps, refresh the branch, then have maintainers/security approve the bundled resolver boundary and plugin policy mutation for the final head.

options.title: Accept bundled Vault deliberately
options.body: Maintainers may keep the branch in core if they explicitly own the credential, dependency, and upgrade-safety risks as a reference Vault integration.

options.title: Keep Vault external
options.body: If Vault should not be core-owned, close or pause this PR and publish the implementation through a plugin/ClawHub path using the existing SecretRef integration seam.

recommendation.title: Clean and security-approve before merge
recommendation.body: Remove the unrelated shrinkwrap bumps, refresh the branch, then have maintainers/security approve the bundled resolver boundary and plugin policy mutation for the final head.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the clearest history on SecretRef and `secrets apply` behavior that this bundled resolver depends on.
